decision: Not adopted: a row saying that Claude Code's grep shell function skips gitignored files, so a recursive grep can print nothing and exit 1 while a match exists.
reopen_if: The grep-ignored-empty-nudge hook is removed or stops firing on an empty recursive grep, or a real session misses a match the hook did not flag.
why: The plugin's grep-ignored-empty-nudge hook already fires at the moment it matters: when a call running a recursive grep prints nothing, it tells the agent to re-run it through bash -c or command grep. The report also came from a scripted probe session, not from a real miss.

decision: Not adopted: a row saying BSD grep (FreeBSD, pfSense, macOS) has no GNU backslash escapes.
reopen_if: compuse-ssh drops that paragraph, or the trap shows up in local shell work with no ssh involved.
why: compuse-ssh already covers it in more detail: grep and sed, the trailing-backslash abort, the quoting layers between the local shell and the remote sh, POSIX classes, and copying the file back to parse it in Python. A remote host is also where the trap bites, so one copy there is enough.

decision: Not adopted: a row warning that awk's END block fires once after every file of a multi-file glob, so a per-file test written in END only sees the last file.
reopen_if: A baseline run without the skill gets awk END over several files wrong.
why: No gap: a clean-room baseline run without the skill, on a neutral task, already explained END, FILENAME, NR versus FNR, and gave both a per-file fix and a gawk ENDFILE form. The row would teach nothing the model does not already do.

anchors: A width cap can cut off the END of a name
decision: Two quick-reference rows: a glob or identifier built from a width-capped listing (cut -c, column) must be read from the uncut field and tested against a control; printf with a float format runs under LC_ALL=C because bash parses its argument by LC_NUMERIC.

evidence.text: printf reproduced locally under de_AT.UTF-8: 0,000, a localized invalid-number message, rc=1; LC_ALL=C prefix printed 0.500. Opus and haiku quote-back on the new rows answered from them.

reopen_if: bash stops parsing printf float arguments by LC_NUMERIC.
why: Both failures were silent in real sessions: an exclude built from a truncated name matched nothing and its dry run looked like the control's; a timing loop under a decimal-comma locale printed 0,000 for every run. Asked directly, opus and haiku baselines knew both facts, so the rows stay one line each and are keyed on the moment of use rather than explaining the mechanism at length.

anchors: Pass `-q` (`tail -q -F A B`: no headers), and take the pattern from the producer's exact output line
decision: A tail -F watch over several logs passes -q and draws its pattern from the producer's exact line, because tail's ==> path <== headers reach grep.

evidence.text: tail -n 1 on two files piped to grep -c counted the 2 header lines; with -q, 0.

reopen_if: tail stops printing headers for multiple files by default.
why: Two queued reports: a watch fired on header lines alone (a pattern word in the path, or the => decoration), and one stayed silent on a pattern the producer never prints.

anchors: The same exit 1 stops a chain: `grep -c PAT f && next_step` prints `0` and silently skips `next_step`
decision: A grep -c count is not chained with && to a next step, since grep exits 1 on a zero count and the chain stops silently.

evidence.text: grep -c zzz f && echo ran printed 0, exit 1, no ran.

reopen_if: grep -c exits 0 on a zero count.
why: A pre-check of the form 'grep -c x f && scp ...' skipped the copy with no error.

decision: Name every tmux session you start and end it with kill-session -t <name>, confirmed by has-session; never kill-server or another session's name.

evidence.text: tmux's default socket is /tmp/tmux-<uid>/default (one server per user); the rule's source fact came from a deep dream (2026-11-19) whose fact body was cut to a pointer. ARGUED, not measured here.

reopen_if: tmux starts giving each client process its own server by default.
why: The tmux server is per user on the host, so kill-server ends other Claude sessions' and the user's tmux sessions.

anchors: Waiting for the next run of a timer's `Type=oneshot` service
decision: A waiter for the next run of a timer's Type=oneshot service records InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic at arming and waits until it differs while ActiveState is inactive or failed; never is-active, ActiveState or Result alone (stale from the previous run), never ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic (stays 0 for a plain oneshot), never ExecMainExitTimestampMonotonic (not set when a start fails before the main process).

evidence.text: Measured 2026-11-20: a transient oneshot sh -c 'sleep 2; exit 3' read activating with ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic, ExecMainExitTimestampMonotonic and InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic all 0, then failed with both per-run properties set, ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic still 0, ExecMainStatus=3, Result=exit-code, InvocationID unchanged since the start. The persistent pve-bindsnap-autovet.service moved both per-run properties across its 20:01 run with ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic 0. RED (opus) on the pre-edit text flagged the systemd-run row's is-active advice as wrong for a unit that ran before. A transient oneshot with ExecStartPre=/bin/false ended failed with InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic set and ExecMainExitTimestampMonotonic=0 (GREEN opus raised it, measured the same day).

reopen_if: systemd starts setting ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic for a oneshot without RemainAfterExit, or a measured run shows InactiveEnterTimestampMonotonic not moving across a run's end.
why: A waiter gated on ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic polled six hours past a finished run of a timer-driven oneshot and had to be stopped by hand; the only oneshot line in the skill sat inside the systemd-run row, written for a transient unit, where its is-active advice is satisfied at once by a persistent unit's stale state.
